extension.description: A heading outline for Jupyter notebooks and Markdown files that opens expanded only to a chosen level.
view.welcome: Open a Jupyter notebook or a Markdown file to see its headings.
config.defaultExpandLevel: Deepest heading level visible when a notebook is opened. Deeper headings are kept but start collapsed (2 = show # and ##, with ## collapsed).
config.numberH1: Also number level-1 (#) headings. Off by default, so a notebook with a single # title numbers its ## headings as 1, 2, 3.
config.followCursor: Highlight the section containing the selected or top visible cell. If that heading is inside a collapsed section, the nearest visible ancestor is highlighted instead (the tree is never expanded for you).
config.showCellCount: Show the number of cells in each section (up to the next heading of the same or a higher level) next to the heading.
config.showOutputSize: Show the total output size of each notebook section (for example "34 · 2.1 MB") next to the heading. Helps find the sections whose outputs make a notebook large or slow to render.
config.levelColors: Color headings by level (## red, ### orange, #### blue, ##### purple, ###### olive). Override colors via workbench.colorCustomizations with the notebookHeadings.levelNForeground keys.
config.markdown: Also show headings for Markdown (.md) files.
config.statusBar: Show the current section in the status bar; click it to open the headings view.
color.level1: Notebook Headings: color of level-1 section headings (red; usually the ## headings).
color.level2: Notebook Headings: color of level-2 section headings (orange; usually the ### headings).
color.level3: Notebook Headings: color of level-3 section headings (blue; usually the #### headings).
color.level4: Notebook Headings: color of level-4 section headings (purple; usually the ##### headings).
color.level5: Notebook Headings: color of level-5 section headings (olive; usually the ###### headings).
color.level6: Notebook Headings: color of level-6 section headings (gray; used for ###### when a document has several # headings).
config.cellTagButton: Show a Tags button at the bottom right of code cells (and of Markdown cells that already have tags). Clicking it opens a checklist of the collapse tags (hide-output, hide-input, hide-cell) to set the cell's tags; this edits only the tags in the cell metadata and can be undone.
